George Frideric Handel composed the music of Messiah in about twenty four days in the late summer of seventeen forty one. It was first performed in Dublin the next spring as a charity concert, helping to free prisoners from debt. The music that proclaims our Redeemer first helped set captives free.

In seventeen twenty seven, the Moravian believers at Herrnhut in Germany began a prayer watch, with someone praying every hour of the day and night. That chain of prayer is said to have continued for about a hundred years. If you are awake and praying tonight, you are keeping a holy watch too.

William Tyndale once said he would cause a boy that drives the plow to know more of the Scripture than the learned men of his day. He gave his life to put the Bible into English. Before he died for his faith, he prayed, Lord, open the King of England's eyes. The Bible you hold tonight cost someone dearly.

Polycarp was an old bishop of Smyrna who had known those who knew the apostles. When told to deny Christ, he answered, eighty and six years have I served Him, and He has done me no wrong. How then can I blaspheme my King who saved me. A long faithful life is a beautiful testimony.

In nineteen forty nine, at a retreat in the California mountains, young Billy Graham was troubled by doubts about the Bible. He walked into the woods, laid his Bible on a tree stump, and prayed that he would accept it by faith as God's Word. Weeks later his Los Angeles crusade began, and his ministry reached the world.

Eric Liddell refused to run an Olympic race on Sunday in nineteen twenty four, then won gold in the four hundred meters. He later served as a missionary in China and died in an internment camp in nineteen forty five. His favorite hymn was Be Still, My Soul. Be still, my soul, the Lord is on thy side.

Susanna Wesley had a house full of children and almost no privacy. So, as her family remembered it, when she needed to pray she would pull her apron up over her head, and the children knew to leave her alone with God. You do not need a quiet chapel. Just a moment, and a heart turned toward Him.

John Bunyan spent about twelve years in the county jail at Bedford for preaching without a license. It was during his imprisonment that he began writing The Pilgrim's Progress, the story of Christian's journey to the Celestial City. A prison cell became the birthplace of one of the most beloved Christian books ever written.

Cecil Frances Alexander wrote Hymns for Little Children in eighteen forty eight, to help children understand the Apostles' Creed. For the line, born of the Virgin Mary, she wrote Once in Royal David's City. For centuries since, it has opened Christmas Eve services with a single child's voice.

In that same little book of hymns for children, Cecil Frances Alexander explained the words, suffered under Pontius Pilate, with the hymn There Is a Green Hill Far Away. Simple words for small hearts. There was no other good enough to pay the price of sin.
reference: There Is a Green Hill Far Away

content: Horatius Bonar, a Scottish minister, began writing hymns for the children in his Sunday school. He went on to write hundreds. One of his best is I Heard the Voice of Jesus Say. Come unto Me and rest. Lay down, thou weary one.
reference: I Heard the Voice of Jesus Say

content: Robert Murray M'Cheyne, a young Scottish pastor, made a calendar in eighteen forty two to help his congregation read through the Bible in a year. He died the next year, at only twenty nine. His reading plan is still used by believers around the world. A short life, faithfully lived, can bear long fruit.

Sir Henry Baker wrote The King of Love My Shepherd Is, a hymn based on Psalm twenty three, in eighteen sixty eight. It is recorded that among his last words were lines from his own third verse, about straying and being gently brought home on the Shepherd's shoulder rejoicing.
reference: The King of Love My Shepherd Is

content: Thomas Aquinas wrote some of the greatest works of theology ever written. But near the end of his life, after an experience of worship, he stopped writing and said that all he had written seemed like straw compared to what he had seen. One glimpse of God is worth more than a library.

In thirteen seventy three, a woman in Norwich, England, now known as Julian of Norwich, was gravely ill and received a series of visions of Christ's love. She wrote that she heard the words, all shall be well, and all shall be well, and all manner of thing shall be well. That is a word for the middle of the night.

Jerome spent many years living in Bethlehem, near the place where Jesus was born, translating the Scriptures into Latin, the common language of his day. His translation served the church for over a thousand years. Quiet, patient work in a little town gave the Word to millions.

The historian Bede tells of Caedmon, a cowherd at the abbey of Whitby who was too shy to sing. One night he slipped out to the cattle shed and fell asleep. In a dream someone asked him to sing of the creation. He did, and woke with the song still in him. God can give a song in the night to the humblest of us.

The Venerable Bede, the old English scholar, spent his last days translating the Gospel of John. As the story was written down by one who was there, a young helper told him one sentence remained. Bede finished it and said, it is finished. Then he sang glory to the Father, and went home to God.

Samuel Morse sent the first long distance telegraph message, from Washington to Baltimore, in eighteen forty four. The words were taken from the book of Numbers. What hath God wrought. A great invention began by giving glory to God.

George Washington Carver, the scientist famous for his work with peanuts and sweet potatoes, rose around four in the morning to walk in the woods. He said that was when he talked with God and listened, and that God showed him things. The early hours can be a holy time.

Florence Nightingale wrote that God spoke to her and called her to His service when she was sixteen. Years later, during the Crimean War, she walked the long hospital wards at night carrying a lamp, checking on wounded soldiers. They called her the Lady with the Lamp. Night nurses, you walk in a noble line.

During the Welsh revival of nineteen oh four, one hymn was sung so often it was called the love song of the revival. Here is love, vast as the ocean, lovingkindness as the flood. Its words were by William Rees. Whole chapels sang it softly, over and over, amazed at the love of God.

In nineteen forty nine, on the Isle of Lewis in Scotland, two sisters named Peggy and Christine Smith, eighty four and eighty two, one blind and one bent with arthritis, prayed late into the night for their village. They clung to Isaiah forty four, I will pour water upon him that is thirsty. A great revival followed.

On September twenty third, eighteen fifty seven, Jeremiah Lanphier, a city missionary in New York, opened a noon prayer meeting on Fulton Street. For a while he prayed alone. By the end only six had come. Within months, thousands across the city were gathering to pray. Never despise small beginnings.

One summer afternoon in eighteen oh six, five students at Williams College in Massachusetts were caught in a thunderstorm and took shelter beside a haystack. There they prayed about carrying the gospel to the nations. That haystack prayer meeting helped launch the American foreign missions movement.

On February third, nineteen seventy, a regular chapel service at Asbury College in Kentucky did not end when it was supposed to. Students quietly confessed and prayed and sang, and the meeting went on around the clock for about a week. No one planned it. God simply came near.

As a young nobleman, Count Zinzendorf stood before a painting of Christ wearing the crown of thorns in an art gallery in Dusseldorf. Beneath it were words that said, this I have done for thee, what hast thou done for Me. He gave his life to Christ's service and later sheltered the Moravian believers on his estate.

A Welsh girl named Mary Jones walked about twenty five miles in the year eighteen hundred to the town of Bala to buy a Bible of her own, after saving for years. Her story moved Thomas Charles and others, and helped lead to the founding of the British and Foreign Bible Society. One girl's hunger for the Word blessed the world.

Robert Raikes, a newspaper publisher in Gloucester, England, saw poor children running wild on the streets in seventeen eighty. He began a school on Sundays to teach them to read, using the Bible. The Sunday school movement spread around the world. Small acts of love can change generations.

The poet William Cowper struggled with deep depression for much of his life. Around seventeen seventy three he wrote God Moves in a Mysterious Way. Ye fearful saints, fresh courage take, the clouds ye so much dread are big with mercy. A man who knew the dark wrote one of the church's most hopeful hymns.
reference: God Moves in a Mysterious Way

content: Elizabeth Fry, a Christian woman in London, visited the women's section of Newgate prison in eighteen thirteen and found mothers and children in terrible conditions. She came back again and again, reading the Bible to them, teaching and caring for them. Jesus said, I was in prison, and ye came unto Me.

David Brainerd was a young missionary to Native Americans in the seventeen forties who often went alone into the woods to pray, sometimes in cold and snow. He died before turning thirty. Jonathan Edwards published his diary, and it inspired generations of missionaries to give their lives to Christ.

At the end of nineteen forty four, Dietrich Bonhoeffer was in prison in Berlin. For his mother and his fiancee he wrote a poem of faith for the new year. By gracious powers so wonderfully sheltered, we wait with confidence, come what may. It has become a beloved hymn of trust in God.

Bill and Gloria Gaither first met as young teachers at the high school in Alexandria, Indiana. Bill taught English, and Gloria taught French. Out of that small town friendship came a marriage and a ministry of songs that has blessed millions, from Because He Lives to the Homecoming gatherings.

Michael W. Smith and his wife Debbie wrote Friends for a man from their Bible study group named Bill, who was moving away. They wrote it quickly and gave it to him as a farewell gift that same evening. A simple goodbye song became a gift to every Christian who has ever had to say farewell to a friend.

Amy Grant and Michael W. Smith wrote Thy Word, which appeared on her album Straight Ahead in nineteen eighty four. It is drawn straight from Psalm one hundred nineteen. Thy word is a lamp unto my feet, and a light unto my path. A little song with an ancient root.

El Shaddai was written by Michael Card and John Thompson and recorded by Amy Grant in nineteen eighty two. The title is a Hebrew name of God often translated God Almighty. The song walks through the Old Testament story of God's faithfulness all the way to Jesus.

Dottie Rambo wrote We Shall Behold Him, and Sandi Patty's soaring performance of it in the early nineteen eighties became one of the best loved moments in Christian music. The song looks forward to the day the sky will unfold and we will see the Lord. What a day that will be.

Easter Song was written by Annie Herring of the Second Chapter of Acts, the singing family group she shared with her brother Matthew Ward and sister Nelly. It is still one of the gladdest songs of the resurrection.

William Williams of Pantycelyn, a Welsh preacher, wrote Guide Me, O Thou Great Jehovah in Welsh in seventeen forty five. Peter Williams translated it into English. It pictures the Christian life as Israel's journey through the wilderness. Bread of heaven, feed me till I want no more.
reference: Guide Me, O Thou Great Jehovah

content: When Martin Luther felt discouraged and under attack, he would remind himself, I am baptized. He did not look to his feelings, but to the promise God had made. When the night is long and your feelings waver, remember whose you are.

Martin Luther wrote From Heaven Above to Earth I Come as a Christmas hymn for his own family. It retells the angel's message to the shepherds and invites children to come and see the baby in the manger. The great Reformer was also a father who loved Christmas Eve at home.
reference: From Heaven Above to Earth I Come

content: On Christmas Eve in nineteen fourteen, in the first winter of the Great War, soldiers in some trenches on the Western Front sang carols across the lines, including Silent Night. In places they met in no man's land and shook hands. For one night, the Prince of Peace was honored even in war.

William Tappan wrote Tis Midnight, and on Olive's Brow in eighteen twenty two. It remembers Jesus praying alone in the garden while His disciples slept. The suffering Savior prays alone, yet He was not forsaken. If you are up at midnight tonight, He knows what that loneliness feels like.
reference: Tis Midnight, and on Olive's Brow

content: Pastor Cleland McAfee wrote Near to the Heart of God after his brother's two little daughters died of diphtheria. Their house was under quarantine, so McAfee and the church choir stood outside in the evening and sang the new hymn to the grieving family. There is a place of quiet rest, near to the heart of God.
reference: Near to the Heart of God

content: On Christmas Day in eighteen sixty three, the poet Henry Wadsworth Longfellow was grieving his wife and worried for his son, wounded in war. He heard the church bells and wrote I Heard the Bells on Christmas Day. God is not dead, nor doth He sleep. The wrong shall fail, the right prevail.
reference: I Heard the Bells on Christmas Day

content: Edward Hopper pastored a church in New York for sailors, and in eighteen seventy one he wrote Jesus, Savior, Pilot Me for them. Chart and compass come from Thee. When the waves of life roll high tonight, the same Savior who stilled Galilee is steering your boat.

The tune we call Old Hundredth comes from the Genevan Psalter of fifteen fifty one, attributed to Louis Bourgeois. It was first sung in English with William Kethe's paraphrase of Psalm one hundred. All people that on earth do dwell, sing to the Lord with cheerful voice. Nearly five centuries of praise on one melody.

The Scottish Psalter of sixteen fifty gave the world a metrical version of Psalm twenty three. The Lord's my shepherd, I'll not want. Today it is often sung to the gentle tune Crimond, named for a village in Scotland. Generations have sung it at weddings, at funerals, and at bedsides.

John Wycliffe, an English scholar of the thirteen hundreds, believed ordinary people should be able to read the Bible in their own language. He and his followers produced the first complete Bible in English, copied by hand. They called him the morning star of the Reformation.

John Wesley rode many thousands of miles on horseback preaching the gospel through England. In seventeen ninety one, as he lay dying at the age of eighty seven, he gathered his strength and said, the best of all is, God is with us. That is the best of all for us tonight too.

D. L. Moody died in December of eighteen ninety nine. Near the end, his family heard him say, earth recedes, heaven opens before me. He told them, if this is death, it is sweet. For the child of God, the last night here is the first morning there.

Isaac Watts wrote a book of songs for children in seventeen fifteen. One was a cradle hymn. Hush, my dear, lie still and slumber, holy angels guard thy bed. Three hundred years later, it is still a lovely blessing to whisper over a sleeping child, or over your own weary heart.

In twelve twenty three, in the Italian village of Greccio, Francis of Assisi set up a manger with an ox and a donkey and invited the villagers to come at night with candles to remember the birth of Christ. That humble scene helped inspire the nativity scenes we still set out today.

Augustine of Hippo opened his book of Confessions with a prayer to God. Thou hast made us for Thyself, and our heart is restless until it rests in Thee. If you are restless tonight, maybe that is the oldest longing of all, the heart looking for home in God.

Edward Bickersteth, an English clergyman, heard a sermon on Isaiah twenty six three, Thou wilt keep him in perfect peace, whose mind is stayed on Thee. He wrote Peace, Perfect Peace in eighteen seventy five. Each verse asks a hard question about life's troubles, and answers with the peace of Jesus.
